title: Linearity and raw rationalization of smooth-adjunction comparison diagrams
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For a finite extension $B/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure write $R_B=\mathcal O_B$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $\mathcal D_B(W)=D^b_c(W,R_B)$ for the derived-complete integral constructible category over the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_{B,W}$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Put $P_B=Rf_{!,R_B}:\mathcal D_B(X)\to\mathcal D_B(Y)$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and $J_B=H_{f,R_B}$ with its tower adjunction $P_B\dashv J_B$, unit $\eta_B^J$, and counit $\epsilon_B^J$ [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. Composition below is right to left.

Let $H_B=Lf^*_{R_B}(-)(d)[2d]$ with pullback and twists of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and let $\gamma_B:H_B\to J_B$ be the specified integral purity isomorphism [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. Use the transported adjunction $P_B\dashv H_B$, whose unit and counit are $\eta_B^H=\gamma_B^{-1}\eta_B^J$ and $\epsilon_B^H=\epsilon_B^J P_B(\gamma_B)$. The integral compact-support functor is the total derived limit of the strict $R_B$-linear compact-support reduction-tower lift [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then $P_B$ is $R_B$-linear, and the integral adjunction bijections and their inverses are $R_B$-linear.

Let $Q_B^W:\mathcal D_B(W)\to\mathcal D_B(W)[1/\varpi_B]=D^b_c(W,B)$ be raw scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], with the same objects and Hom modules $\operatorname{Hom}(U,V)\otimes_{R_B}B$. The localized functors $P_{B,\mathrm{rat}},H_{B,\mathrm{rat}}$ are rational compact supports and twisted pullback. The tensor of the integral Hom bijection is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P_{B,\mathrm{rat}}M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,H_{B,\mathrm{rat}}K).$$
It is natural for every rational morphism, has unit $Q_B^X(\eta_B^H)$ and counit $Q_B^Y(\epsilon_B^H)$, and hence specifies the scalar-localized smooth adjunction.

Let $E\subset F$ be finite coefficient fields and $C^W_{F/E}$ the completed integral coefficient extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Suppose natural integral isomorphisms
$$b^0:C^Y_{F/E}P_E\to P_FC^X_{F/E},\qquad a^0:C^X_{F/E}H_E\to H_FC^Y_{F/E}$$
are given, satisfying
$$H_F(b^0_M)a^0_{P_EM}C^X_{F/E}(\eta_E^H(M))=\eta_F^H(C^X_{F/E}M),$$
$$\epsilon_F^H(C^Y_{F/E}K)P_F(a^0_K)b^0_{H_EK}=C^Y_{F/E}(\epsilon_E^H(K)).$$
Define $b_{F/E,Q_EM_0}=Q_F^Y(b^0_{M_0})$ and $a_{F/E,Q_EK_0}=Q_F^X(a^0_{K_0})$. These are natural isomorphisms for the rational coefficient functor $-\otimes_EF$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with inverse components $Q_F((b^0)^{-1})$, $Q_F((a^0)^{-1})$. Naturality holds for every finite sum of pure tensors $u\otimes\lambda$, $\lambda\in E\subset F$, in the rational Hom modules, including rational isomorphisms between integral representatives. They satisfy the displayed unit/counit identities with every functor, unit and counit rationalized.

If the integral $a^0,b^0$ for every $E\subset F\subset L$ satisfy their coefficient cocycles with the completed-extension associators whose rationalizations are [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], their localized images satisfy the same cocycles with these rational associators. Identity-extension comparisons remain identities. These assertions use only raw scalar localization; no idempotent completion or lift of a rational isomorphism to an integral isomorphism is required.

The relation with the rational-purity unit is explicit: in the condensed rational realization of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], identify the integral constructible category with the derived-complete category as in that theorem. Let $\rho_W$ be its natural $B$-linear Hom comparison $h\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda h[1/\ell]$, and use its specified rational pullback and compact-support comparisons; on the compact-support side identify $P_B$ with the ambient composite $R\bar f_*j_!$ by the canonical isomorphism of clause (2) of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower], and on the twisted-pullback side compose with the canonical associativity isomorphism $(N[1/\ell])(d)[2d]\cong(N(d)[2d])[1/\ell]$ of derived tensor products, the twist being tensor with the invertible Tate-twist sheaf of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Under these endpoint comparisons the transported adjunction Hom bijection is exactly $\rho_X\circ(\Phi_B^H\otimes1)\circ\rho_Y^{-1}$, where $\Phi_B^H$ is the integral $P_B\dashv H_B$ bijection. In particular the raw tensor-localized bijection above and the localized-Hom construction in the rational-purity unit agree under the displayed Hom comparisons; this is an equality of bijections with the specified endpoints, not a definition equating raw and condensed coefficient categories.

proof.text: Put $R=R_B$ and let $\mathcal A$ be the category of modules over $\widehat R_{B,Y}$. Give strict towers the componentwise $R$-action. Their category is abelian by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The ordinary inverse-limit functor $U:\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A$ is $R$-linear: composing $U(v+w)$ and $U(v)+U(w)$ with every limit projection gives the same map, and likewise for $U(rv)$ and $rU(v)$; uniqueness in the limit universal property proves equality. The stipulated total derived limit has the K-injective tower computation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], in particular K-injective tower resolutions exist in these module-sheaf categories. The induced derived linear structures are those of [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. Apply [lem-weil-kinjective-total-derived-linear] to this $U$; no exactness of $U$ is needed. Thus $R\lim$ is $R$-linear. The strict compact-support lift $\mathcal T_f$ is $R$-linear by [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor]. By the integral construction specified in the hypotheses, $P_B=(R\lim)\mathcal T_f$ on the constructible subcategories. Composing the two linear maps on Hom modules proves that $P_B$ is $R$-linear. A specified natural identification with this composite preserves linearity by conjugation with its components.

proof.text: Use the given tower adjunction and its natural purity isomorphism $\gamma:H_B\xrightarrow{\sim}J_B$ from [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. By [lem-sbc-linear-right-adjoint], Step 1 implies that $J_B$ is $R_B$-linear. For an integral arrow $h:K\to K'$, naturality of $\gamma$ gives $H_B(h)=\gamma_{K'}^{-1}J_B(h)\gamma_K$, so bilinearity of composition makes $H_B$ linear as well. Write $\Phi^J(u)=J_B(u)\eta^J_M$ and $(\Phi^J)^{-1}(v)=\epsilon^J_KP_B(v)$. These formulas follow by evaluating the two naturality squares of the adjunction at identity arrows. Both maps are linear by linearity of the functors and bilinearity of composition. Transport through $\gamma$ gives $\Phi^H(u)=\gamma_K^{-1}\Phi^J(u)$ and $(\Phi^H)^{-1}(v)=(\Phi^J)^{-1}(\gamma_Kv)$. Consequently both maps are linear, and evaluation at identities gives precisely $\eta^H_M=\gamma_{P_BM}^{-1}\eta^J_M$ and $\epsilon^H_K=\epsilon^J_KP_B(\gamma_K)$.

proof.text: For an integral $R_B$-linear functor $F$, use the semilinear extension of [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] with the identity coefficient homomorphism. Uniqueness of the coefficient map identifies it with the identity of the localized coefficient ring, so the chosen additive Hom extension sends $a\otimes u$ to $a\otimes F(u)$. Tensor induction proves scalar linearity over the localized ring. Define the rational unit and counit to be $1\otimes\eta^H$ and $1\otimes\epsilon^H$. For $a\otimes f$ with integral $f:M\to N$, unit naturality is $a\otimes(\eta_N^H\circ f)=a\otimes(H_BP_B(f)\circ\eta_M^H)$, by integral naturality; prove the counit equation in the same way. Additivity extends both equations to every rational arrow. The two rational triangle equations are $1$ tensored with the integral triangles, using the composition law of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. These explicit transformations and triangles construct an adjunction between the actual localized $P_B$ and $H_B$.

proof.text: Compute both Hom directions of this adjunction from their unit and counit formulas. The forward map sends $a\otimes u$ to $a\otimes(H_B(u)\circ\eta_M^H)$; its inverse sends $a\otimes v$ to $a\otimes(\epsilon_K^H\circ P_B(v))$. These are precisely the specified integral adjuncts tensored with $a$. Additivity follows from the additive right adjoint, and scalar linearity follows from its localized linearity and bilinear composition. Thus the Hom bijections agree on every tensor with the tensor of the integral linear Hom equivalence of Step 2, using [def-weil-module-base-change]. The unit and counit are exactly $Q_B(\eta^H)$ and $Q_B(\epsilon^H)$, since $Q_B$ sends an integral arrow to that arrow tensored with $1$. The categories and functors are precisely the raw rationalization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the stated twisted pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. No objects or idempotents are adjoined.

proof.text:
For $E\subset F$, the integral functor $C^W=C^W_{F/E}$ is additive and semilinear for $R_E\to R_F$ by [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. The image of $\varpi_E$ is nonzero in the field $F$, hence invertible there. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to $C^Y P_E,P_F C^X$ and to $C^X H_E,H_F C^Y$, using Steps 1--2. Its extended transformations have components $Q_F^Y(b^0_M)$ and $Q_F^X(a^0_K)$, and the extended coefficient functor is exactly $-\otimes_EF$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Explicitly, for an integral $u:M\to N$ and $\lambda\in E$, the naturality equation for $b$ is
$$P_{F,\mathrm{rat}}\overline C^X(u\otimes\lambda)b_M=\lambda Q_F^Y(P_FC^X(u)b^0_M)=\lambda Q_F^Y(b^0_NC^YP_E(u))=b_N\overline C^YP_{E,\mathrm{rat}}(u\otimes\lambda).$$
The identical calculation with $(C^XH_E,H_FC^Y,a^0)$ proves naturality of $a$. Linearity gives the equations for every finite sum of pure tensors. Applying $Q_F$ to $b^0(b^0)^{-1}=1=(b^0)^{-1}b^0$ and to the two corresponding equations for $a^0$ gives the stated inverse components.

proof.text:
Localization preserves whiskering, vertical composition and equations of semilinear transformations by [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization]. In particular, using the object identifications of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], the rationalized unit composite is
$$H_{F,\mathrm{rat}}(b_M)a_{P_{E,\mathrm{rat}}M}\overline C^X(\eta^H_{E,\mathrm{rat},M})=Q_F^X\bigl(H_F(b^0_M)a^0_{P_EM}C^X(\eta_E^H(M))\bigr)=Q_F^X(\eta_F^H(C^XM)).$$
The analogous counit composite is
$$\epsilon^H_{F,\mathrm{rat},\overline C^YK}P_{F,\mathrm{rat}}(a_K)b_{H_{E,\mathrm{rat}}K}=Q_F^Y\bigl(\epsilon_F^H(C^YK)P_F(a^0_K)b^0_{H_EK}\bigr)=Q_F^Y(C^Y(\epsilon_E^H(K))).$$
The final terms are the localized unit and the coefficient extension of the localized counit by Step 4. This proves both displayed comparison identities with their specified orientations.

proof.text:
For $E\subset F\subset L$ denote the given integral coefficient associator by $c^W:C^W_{L/F}C^W_{F/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}C^W_{L/E}$. For compact supports the assumed integral cocycle reads
$$P_L(c^X_M)b^0_{L/F,C^X_{F/E}M}C^Y_{L/F}(b^0_{F/E,M})=b^0_{L/E,M}c^Y_{P_EM}.$$
Apply $Q_L^Y$ to this equality. Preservation of composition and whiskering in [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] identifies each factor with its rationalized factor, giving the required rational compact-support cocycle. The assumed twisted-pullback equation is
$$H_L(c^Y_K)a^0_{L/F,C^Y_{F/E}K}C^X_{L/F}(a^0_{F/E,K})=a^0_{L/E,K}c^X_{H_EK};$$
applying $Q_L^X$ gives its rational cocycle by the same factor-by-factor identification. The hypothesis identifies $Q_L(c^W)$ with the associator of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], so these are the specified associators. For identity extensions, $Q_E(1)=1$ proves the normalization. Finally, if a localized arrow is an isomorphism, the naturality equation of Step 5 holds for it and for its inverse, since both belong to the localized Hom modules. No integral inverse is used.

proof.text:
For the last assertion, identify the integral categories as required in [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], and send an unchanged integral object $N$ to $N[1/\ell]$ in its condensed rational realization. On Hom modules send $h\otimes\lambda$ to $\rho_W(h\otimes\lambda)=\lambda h[1/\ell]$. The cited statement says that this is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism. It preserves identities; on two composable pure tensors,
$$\rho_W((v\otimes\mu)(u\otimes\lambda))=\mu\lambda(vu)[1/\ell]=(\mu v[1/\ell])(\lambda u[1/\ell]).$$
Additivity gives preservation of composition for arbitrary arrows. Thus these maps define a fully faithful functor from raw localization into the condensed category. The same cited statement gives an integral model for every condensed constructible rational object. In particular every change between two such representatives is represented by a rational arrow via $\rho_W$, and an invertible change is represented by a rational isomorphism, by full faithfulness. This is an explicit comparison of categories and maps, rather than an identification by definition.

proof.text: Use the natural compact-support comparison of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom]. Its integral endpoint is the ambient composite $R\bar f_*j_!$; compose with the canonical integral comparison of clause (2) of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower] to obtain the stated endpoint for $P_B$. For twisted pullback, first use the pullback comparison of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], then commute scalar extension past the twist by [lem-pur-ordinary-line-derived-scalar-comparison]. Apply that lemma to $R_0=\widehat R_{B,X}$, its rational coefficient ring $R_1$, and $R_2=R_1$ with identity last map. Take $L_0$ to be the integral Tate line and $L_1$ its scalar extension, with multiplication as the identity comparison. These are locally rank-one sheaves and have the required tensor-power comparisons by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]; $m=d$ gives the twist needed here. The canonical shift comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-tensor-additive-constraints] then commute this scalar tensor past $[2d]$. On K-flat representatives this endpoint map is the unsigned reassociation of the scalar factor and the degree-zero Tate factor, followed by the canonical shift reindexing. Consequently the twisted-pullback endpoint is precisely $(N[1/\ell])(d)[2d]\cong(N(d)[2d])[1/\ell]$ specified in the item, natural in $N$.

proof.text: With the endpoint comparisons of Step 9 inserted, an arbitrary arrow in the source Hom module has a unique expression $\rho_Y(z)$ with $z\in\operatorname{Hom}(P_BM,K)\otimes_{R_B}B$, by [det-sp-rational-localized-hom]. For $z=u\otimes\lambda$, the three arrows in the localized-Hom construction send it to $u\otimes\lambda$, then to $\Phi_B^H(u)\otimes\lambda$, then to $\lambda\Phi_B^H(u)[1/\ell]=\rho_X((\Phi_B^H\otimes1)(z))$. The middle map is the integral bijection of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection] transported through its specified $\gamma$ as in Step 2. Additivity proves the same identity for every $z$. Hence the transported Hom bijection is exactly $\rho_X(\Phi_B^H\otimes1)\rho_Y^{-1}$. Naturality from Step 3 and naturality of both endpoint comparisons show this equality also after any rational change of representatives; inverses are rational arrows by Step 8. Evaluating at identities recovers the same units and counits as Step 4, and the two inverse bijections give the transported triangle identities. This is exactly the three-bijection normalization in the current rational-purity proof.
